newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks end down on HUBCO, PTCL selling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks end down on HUBCO, PTCL selling.

text.p: Pakistani stocks ended sharply down on Wednesday on heavy selling of Hub Power and PTCL shares by foreign investors amid a depressed economic outlook and political unrest, dealers said.

The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index ended 18.83 points, or 1.36 percent, down at 1,362.80 with 144 losers and 81 gainers. The selling pressure in the two scrips, which carry a heavy weight on the index, neutralised good corporate announcements, broker Majid Chapra said. Foreign sellers did not give the reason for the selling but dealers attributed it to poor economic outlook and political unrest, he said.

Millat tractors announced 75 percent cash dividend per 10-rupee share and HBL Modaraba 20 percent per 10-rupee share for the year ended on June 30, and NDLC 30 percent per five-rupee share for 18 months ended on June 30.
HUBCO fell 1.00 to 31 rupees, PTCL 0.45 to 31.25, Lever Bros 12 to 635 and Fauji Fertilizer 0.35 to 70.25.
